summary: The first mismatch is in the grave-dig branch: C calls dig_up_grave(cc), whose first state/RNG effect is exercise(A_WIS, FALSE), while the JavaScript dighole() branch records note_unported("dig.c dig_up_grave") and returns. This omits the Wisdom exercise and the helper’s role/alignment messages, grave outcome, tile cleanup, engraving removal, and redraw. The existing attrib.c exercise() port already implements the required rn2(2) draw; the source owner is the whole dig.c dig_up_grave() function and its dighole() caller wiring.

source.branch: In dighole(), when old_typ is a grave, C first calls digactualhole(..., PIT), then dig_up_grave(cc). This case reaches the hero-tile path (cc == NULL) as a lawful Archeologist; because the grave is not marked empty, dig_up_grave() draws rn2(5), with the recorded result selecting the unoccupied-grave message.
callers: C: dig.c:dighole() (883-1024), IS_GRAVE(old_typ) branch at 959-962, calls dig_up_grave(cc); the production path reaches dighole() from dig.c:dig() after the downward-dig occupation reaches its effort threshold.
JavaScript: js/dig.js:dighole() partial port, IS_GRAVE(oldType) branch at 1292-1295, calls digactualhole() then note_unported("dig.c dig_up_grave"); replace this gap with the ported helper call.
dependencies: attrib.c:exercise (already ported in js/attrib.js; false Wisdom exercise updates AEXE and consumes rn2(2), the first mismatching C draw).
attrib.c:adjalign (already ported in js/attrib.js; used by the Archeologist, Samurai, and lawful branches).
mkobj.c:mk_tt_object (already ported in js/mkroom.js; the corpse branch checks and ages its returned object).
makemon.c:mkclass (already ported in js/makemon.js) and makemon.c:makemon (already ported in js/makemon_create.js; mkclass supplies the species and makemon’s result is discarded).
engrave.c:del_engr_at and display.c:newsym (already ported in js/engrave.js and js/display.js; required for the final grave cleanup and map redraw).

evidence: The selected v14 manifest entry records archeologist-lawful-digs-grave as reaching dig.c:use_pick_axe -> digactualhole -> dig_up_grave; its C outcome is the grave-robber warning followed by “The grave is unoccupied. Strange...”. The recording has 23 steps and the queue/evaluation report 5 unmatched screens.

The assigned scanner trace .cache/synthetic-scans/v14/archeologist-lawful-digs-grave.json and saved queue entry .cache/v14-baseline-work-queue.json place the first mismatch at step 17, key space: C calls rn2(2)=0 from exercise(attrib.c:509), while JS calls rn2(5)=2; the first screen cell and cursor also differ. The later C grave draw is recorded as rn2(5)=4 at dig_up_grave(dig.c:1058).

nethack-c/upstream/src/dig.c:959-962 establishes the direct IS_GRAVE caller. The whole helper at dig.c:1026-1088 calls exercise(A_WIS, FALSE) at 1044 before role/alignment effects, then selects the grave outcome at 1058 and resets typ/emptygrave/disturbed, deletes the engraving, and redraws at 1083-1087.

nethack-c/upstream/src/attrib.c:488-518 shows that exercise() uses rn2(2) for a false Wisdom exercise when |AEXE(WIS)| < 50. The frozen JavaScript implementation is js/attrib.js:946-994; the missing behavior is its call from dig_up_grave(), not exercise() itself.

Frozen examined source at 3212f9f07c3fdf3f00c5c204885f51834f0b6448: js/dig.js:1292-1295 contains note_unported("dig.c dig_up_grave") immediately after digactualhole(), confirming the source gap and production wiring point.
